claims.text: Warm sessions serialize per session key: exactly one in-flight invocation per continuation ref — concurrent work items sharing a session_key either queue behind the active turn or deliberately fork a fresh session (recorded as such), because codex exec resume / claude --resume assume single-threaded conversations and the bridges' async runners spawn unbounded today

honesty_conditions.text: two simultaneous dispatches with the same session key never produce interleaved turns on one provider thread — pinned by a bridge test

claims.text: Breaker and pacing decisions are observable and reversible: pausing an actor emits an engine event (visible on the dashboard and in Discord), the paused-until state renders on the actors surface, and an operator can clear a pause early via the API/CLI — budget.go's own argument (a silent skip 'stays ready forever and nothing anywhere records why') applies to the breaker exactly

honesty_conditions.text: a tripped breaker is diagnosable from the dashboard alone within one glance (which actor, why, until when) and clearable without touching the database

claims.text: Budget accounting distinguishes cold starts from resumed turns: budget.max_sessions counts NEW provider sessions, and a resumed warm turn charges differently — otherwise stickiness (c3) and the economic contract (c6) fight each other, since a workstream of N node turns on one warm session would count as N sessions and always exhaust the budget it was designed to conserve

honesty_conditions.text: a workstream of node turns sharing one warm session consumes 1 from max_sessions, not N — pinned by an engine test

claims.text: The observe declaration maps observed states to outcomes explicitly, and v1 auto-completes only the merged state (observe: {kind: github_pr_merged, pr: N} -> outcome merged): a PR closed without merging stays on the manual lane (the operator decides dropped vs retry), because #54's own override list names dropped and merge-without-PR as human-judgment cases — the tracker never guesses an outcome from an ambiguous external state

honesty_conditions.text: a PR closed unmerged does NOT auto-complete its task; only the merged state produces an automatic submission — pinned by a tracker test

claims.text: Auto-refresh shares one event stream: the app opens a single app-wide EventSource (a shared provider/context over the cross-run feed) that views subscribe to, instead of each view opening its own — browsers cap concurrent connections per origin (6 on HTTP/1.1), and Mesh + RunView already hold two; per-view EventSources across seven more views would starve the cap in multi-tab use

honesty_conditions.text: opening every dashboard view across two tabs holds at most one SSE connection per tab, and view-level subscriptions attach/detach without reconnecting the stream

claims.text: Parallel tokens ship in full (#43, per q8): the engine honors limits.maxParallelTokens, transition plans grow multi-edge splits and join barriers with per-token bounds, and event-driven continuation lands whole — a node emits events non-blocking mid-execution and any subscribed node picks them up, including as splits; the c9 groundwork (token parent links, multi-waiter signal_subscriptions) is the substrate, and event-then-subscription replay (the 0016 documented gap) is closed as part of this

honesty_conditions.text: a workflow declaring maxParallelTokens > 1 demonstrably runs concurrent tokens through a split and reconverges at a join with bounds enforced, and an event emitted mid-execution resumes a waiter that subscribed AFTER emission (replay closed) — both pinned by engine tests
